subject: Latency spike after model v2.1 A/B rollout — immediate support requested
messages:
From: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@clearview-ai.com
Date: 2026-05-17T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in tail latency at ~08:30 PT after your team pushed model v2.1 into the A portion of our A/B split. P95 is up ~270ms and p99 has increased by ~1.1s; we're also seeing a 1.8% rise in 503 errors and a reduction in sustained throughput for short prompts. This is affecting our chat UI and downstream billing windows.

Attached are the request logs for the affected timeframe (request_logs_20260517.zip). We rolled forward the change on our side and validated config — the traffic split shows the change landed and the regression coincides with the rollout. Can you confirm whether the rollout included any tokenizer or batching changes? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can revert to the previous model variant for all traffic.

This is high priority for us — we're prepared to pause production reads if you recommend a rollback. Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Andrea
Andrea Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearView AI
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, hiro_tanaka@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T09:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Andrea — thanks for the signal and for the logs. I'm escalating to SRE and account so we can move fast. Ben (AE) is on the thread to coordinate the rollback/communications; Marissa (SRE lead) and Hiro (Product) are joining for triage.

Immediate plan:
- Marissa to triage and confirm root cause and whether this is specific to short prompts.
- If we confirm model v2.1 changes are the cause, we will flip the A/B split to 100% previous variant within the hour (unless you request otherwise).
- We'll push a short incident note and keep you updated every 30 mins until stable.

Can you confirm if you want us to proceed with a full rollback to the prior model (v2.0) or prefer a progressive reduction of canary traffic? Grace will wait for SRE recommendation and your approval before making the change.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, hiro_tanaka@redwoodinference.com, andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com
Date: 2026-05-17T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production latency — model rollout impact

Hi team / Andrea — quick triage update from SRE:
- Symptom: p95/p99 latency increase and small uptick in 503s, concentrated on requests with short input length (< 32 tokens).
- Root cause (prelim): v2.1 introduced a tokenizer alignment change and an extra pre-tokenization normalization step that increases micro-batching variance; combined with our continuous-batching policy this caused more KV cache misses for short prefixes and increased end-to-end generation time.
- Evidence: correlated spikes with higher average per-request kernel time in profiling dump (profiling_dump_0517.txt).

Mitigation options:
  1) Immediate: flip the A/B split back to 0% v2.1 (full rollback to v2.0). This is a config change and we can do it in ~8–12 minutes, then monitor for normalization.
  2) Alternative: reduce concurrency and enforce smaller batch windows for the affected shard — buys time but may reduce throughput.
  3) Code path: revert the tokenizer normalization in v2.1 and run a fast canary; nontrivial and will take hours.

Recommendation: execute option 1 now, then reopen a postmortem to validate the tokenization path. I can prepare the canary_policy_diff.patch to force the split to 0% and a short rollback plan; need Grace/Ben approval to flip.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, hiro_tanaka@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Andrea — thanks for raising this and for the logs. We've got an SRE recommendation to roll back v2.1 for your account. With your go-ahead we'll execute the rollback and update you with a timeline; target is to complete the flip and validate within 30 minutes, monitor for 60 minutes, then confirm.

If you're comfortable, we'll proceed with immediate rollback to v2.0. Otherwise we can do a progressive traffic reduction. Please reply "rollback now" to authorize.

I'll also loop in our engineering execs for visibility if you'd like an executive update once stable.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, hiro_tanaka@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Rollback now. Please proceed and confirm when traffic is back on v2.0; we'll validate from our side and report behavior. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Andrea
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T10:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production latency — model rollout impact

Action taken: applied canary_policy_diff.patch; set v2.1 split to 0% for ClearView account at 10:47 PT. Rolling metrics show p95 returning to baseline; p99 trending down but will need 30–45 mins of sampling to be confident. 503 rate back to normal.

Next:
- Monitoring window: 45–60 mins with 30-min check-in.
- Post-incident: we will open a joint postmortem and schedule a patch for v2.1 tokenization path.

Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Andrea — confirming rollback completed and initial monitoring looks good. Can you validate on your side and let us know if anything persistent remains? We'll keep the incident open and provide a final postmortem and timeline for the tokenization fix.

Ben
From: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact

Looks stable from our dashboards — p95/p99 back in normal ranges and throughput recovered. Thanks for the rapid response and clear plan. We'll await the postmortem and the follow-up patch plan before you resume any non-urgent rollouts.

Andrea
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Morales <andrea.morales@clearview-ai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, hiro_tanaka@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-18T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — model rollout impact — postmortem follow-up

Andrea — following up with the postmortem link and our remediation timeline. We identified the tokenizer alignment normalization as the root trigger and will:
- Back out the normalization from v2.1 and run a limited internal canary (no customer traffic) by 2026-05-20.
- Add an additional token-length affinity test in our rollout gating to prevent this regression for short prompts.
- Share a joint postmortem doc (link above) and a timeline for re-release.

Appreciate your partnership and apologies for the disruption. If you want an exec-level summary for your stakeholders we can prepare that and include our SLA credit proposal if it's helpful.

Best,
Grace
